themes_detail.label: Electrical System Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints spiked to 6 this week compared to a 0.4-per-week average over the prior 8 weeks (1500% increase, z-score 11.62)—the highest-severity statistical anomaly in the dataset. This week's surge suggests an emerging infrastructure or safety problem affecting multiple buildings across Bay Ridge/Dyker Heights.
evidence: 6 electrical complaints filed this week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1500% spike)
Z-score of 11.62 indicates this is the most statistically significant spike in the entire 90-day dataset
Spike is brand-new—appearing only in the most recent reporting week
reporting_angles: Interview Con Edison about grid issues, power outages, or equipment failures affecting the neighborhood this week
Contact FDNY and DOB to determine if any electrical fires, hazards, or building code violations are driving complaints

themes_detail.label: Illegal Fireworks Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Illegal fireworks complaints jumped to 4 this week from a 0.9-per-week baseline (357% increase, z-score 4.0), marking a sudden surge in safety and noise violations. This week's spike suggests organized or concentrated illegal pyrotechnic activity in the district.
evidence: 4 illegal fireworks complaints filed this week vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (357% increase)
Z-score of 4.0 indicates statistically significant spike
Surge is acute and brand-new—concentrated entirely in this week's data
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD and 77th Precinct about enforcement actions, arrests, or patterns behind this week's surge
Document resident complaints about noise, safety fears, and impact on families and pets

themes_detail.label: Dead Animal Cleanup Backlog
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints spiked to 17 two weeks ago from a 2.4-per-week baseline (616% increase, z-score 5.86), suggesting a potential public health, sanitation, or wildlife management problem that may still be unresolved. This marks a significant spike from 2 weeks ago that warrants investigation into whether conditions have improved.
evidence: 17 dead animal complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 2.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (616% spike)
Z-score of 5.86 indicates statistically significant cluster event
Second-highest severity spike in the dataset, suggesting either localized wildlife die-off or systemic cleanup delays
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Sanitation and Parks to determine if there was a die-off event, disease outbreak, or service backlog 2 weeks ago
Interview residents about ongoing rodent, pigeon, or wildlife issues; assess whether the spike has resolved

themes_detail.label: Door/Window Damage Wave
themes_detail.summary: Door and window complaints surged to 22 last week compared to a 6.1-per-week average (259% increase, z-score 4.66), suggesting either a break-in pattern, weather damage, or building security breach affecting multiple residences this week or last.
evidence: 22 door/window complaints filed last week vs. 6.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (259% increase)
Z-score of 4.66 indicates statistically significant spike
Pattern could indicate property crime (burglaries), severe weather, or structural issues affecting multiple buildings
reporting_angles: Contact NYPD 77th Precinct to determine if there is a recent burglary or break-in pattern
Interview residents and building owners about weather, security concerns, or maintenance issues; assess whether complaints are related to a specific incident or dispersed across the neighborhood

themes_detail.label: Street Sign Infrastructure Decay
themes_detail.summary: Missing street sign complaints jumped to 5 three weeks ago from a 0.8-per-week baseline (567% increase, z-score 6.43), indicating potential traffic safety hazards and wayfinding problems that may persist. This three-week-old spike warrants follow-up to determine if signs have been replaced.
evidence: 5 missing street sign complaints filed 3 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (567% spike)
Z-score of 6.43 indicates statistically significant spike
Spike is slightly older (3 weeks) than the electrical or fireworks emergencies, warranting verification of current status
reporting_angles: Check with NYC Department of Transportation on sign replacement timelines and whether complaints from 3 weeks ago have been addressed
Document which streets are affected and whether missing signs pose traffic or pedestrian safety risks
